## Dependency status on this machine

- ripgrep, jq, claude CLI: installed
- **yq**: missing — `brew install yq` (required, mikefarah/yq v4)
- **gitleaks**: missing — `brew install gitleaks` (or the script falls back to Docker)

## Design recap (what each piece does)

- `audit-history.sh [target]` mirror-clones the target, runs gitleaks across all refs, then iterates `rules.yaml` + `personal-identifiers.yaml` driving ripgrep with PCRE2. Captured match values are redacted to `[REDACTED:len=N]` before they hit the report. Emits `audit-out/<repo>-<utc>/{gitleaks.json,grep-findings.json,audit-report.json,audit-report.md}`. Exit code 1 on any finding.
- `audit-suggest.sh [target] --last-report <report.json>` builds a redacted fingerprint (paths, manifests, README, CLAUDE.md only — never file content), feeds it plus `archetypes.md` and `rules.yaml` to `claude -p`, extracts the yaml-fenced response into `suggested-rules.yaml`. Has a defensive check that refuses to send a `last-report` whose snippets don't look redacted. `personal-identifiers.yaml` is **not** sent unless you pass `--include-personal`.
- Targets work as local path, remote URL, or `owner/repo` shorthand via `gh`.
